claim: Workers apply on the Sahel Individuals app or PAM's Ashal portal and employers approve on Sahel Business or Ashal
quote: Applications can be submitted and approved through the "Sahel Individuals" mobile app or the "Ashal" Manpower portal. Employers must approve the request via "Sahel Business" or the corporate version of "Ashal"

claim: PAM's director general said a worker whose employer unjustifiably refuses or delays the permit can complain to the labour relations unit linked to the company's file
quote: if an employer unjustifiably refuses or delays granting permission, the worker has the right to file a complaint with the relevant labor relations unit linked to the company’s file

claim: There is no annual limit on exit permits if the employer approves
quote: there is no limit to the number of exit permits that can be issued annually, provided the employer grants approval

claim: In Sahel: Services, Public Authority of Manpower, Expatriate Workers Services, Exit Permit; enter departure and return dates and submit for employer approval
quote: Under “Expatriate Workers Services,” users will find the Exit Permit option, where they can input their intended departure and return dates and submit the request for employer approval.

claim: Apply no earlier than seven days and no later than 24 hours before departure
quote: applications must be submitted no earlier than seven days and no later than 24 hours before the intended departure

claim: To request a permit, log into Sahel, go to Services and select the Public Authority of Manpower
quote: To request a permit, users must log into Sahel, navigate to the Services section, and select the Public Authority of Manpower (PAM).

claim: A worker without a smartphone or in an emergency can have the employer apply for the exit permit on Sahel Business or Ashal; the permit can be used for up to 7 days
quote: Employers can apply on behalf of the worker in cases where the worker has no app access, no smartphone, or during emergencies.

claim: An approved exit permit can be used for up to 7 days from issue
quote: can be used for up to 7 days from the date of issue

claim: PAM recommends printing the permit before travel in case the airline asks; it can also be shown in the Sahel app
quote: PAM recommends that workers print a hard copy of the permit before traveling, in case it is requested by the airlines

claim: In an emergency, the time to get a permit depends on how fast the employer approves
quote: the time needed to obtain a permit ( especially in emergencies) depends primarily on the speed of employer approval

claim: Domestic workers do not need an exit permit
quote: Domestic workers, who are typically subject to stricter mobility restrictions, do not require an exit permit.

claim: Local media reported sponsors demanding around KD 50 from free-visa workers to issue an exit permit
quote: sponsors have demanded around KD 50(US$170) to issue an exit permit to these workers

claim: The Sahel app is only in English and Arabic
quote: is only available in English and Arabic

claim: Many contracts illegally require workers to compensate the employer for resigning before the contract ends
quote: many employment contracts in Kuwait illegally stipulate that workers must compensate their employers for breaching contract terms, such as resigning before the contract period ends

claim: Passport confiscation remains widespread and illegal
quote: remains a widespread practice that is illegal but persists

claim: Since March 2026 employers file absence reports electronically on PAM's As'hal portal; the worker gets an As'hal app alert and has 60 days to contest it with the Labour Relations Department
quote: employees receive instant As'hal app notifications and have 60 days to contest with the Labor Relations Department

claim: The printed absence notice is valid 3 working days, within which the employer must file it with MOI's Residency Affairs Directorate
quote: Printed notifications expire after 3 working days and must be filed with the Ministry of Interior's Residency Affairs Directorate within that window to finalize absence procedures.

claim: The employer must file the absence report with MOI within 15 days of the first day of unnotified absence
quote: The employer must submit an official absence (absconding) report to the Ministry of Interior (MOI) within fifteen (15) days from the first day of the worker’s unnotified absence.

claim: Some managers file false absconding reports to intimidate workers, and visa traders file them to free up quotas for resale
quote: brokers sell work permits to unsuspecting expats and later file absconding cases in bad faith to free up visa quotas for further illegal sale

claim: The employer can withdraw the report via PAM's portal; the worker may object at the Labour Relations Department that the absence was justified or misreported
quote: The employee may file a formal objection at the Labor Relations Department, asserting that the absence was either justified or misreported.

claim: A joint PAM-MOI panel may drop a case if the employer withdraws and agrees to renew or transfer, or the report is malicious, fraudulent or in error
quote: The report is deemed malicious, fraudulent, or filed in error (e.g., during a visa transfer process).

claim: The employer can withdraw the report via PAM's portal
quote: The employer retains the right to cancel or withdraw the report via PAM’s portal.

claim: Administrative Decision 680 of 2026, published in Kuwait Alyoum, amends Decision 842 of 2015 on transfers so PAM can allow transfer before one year in specific cases
quote: Administrative Decision No. (680) of 2026, issued by the Ministry of Manpower, amends certain provisions of Administrative Decision No. (842) of 2015 governing the transfer of workers from one employer to another.

claim: Early transfer grounds: employer fails to issue residency/work permit through negligence; employer file suspended; false or malicious report against the worker; employer breaches Law 6/2010 so the worker may quit without notice (non-payment, abuse, unsafe work, fraud, false criminal charge); bankruptcy or permanent closure
quote: A false or malicious termination report has been filed against the worker, or reporting procedures are misused to harm the worker or block their rights.

claim: Early transfer is allowed when the employer violates Law 6/2010 in ways that let the worker quit without notice, such as non-payment of wages
quote: The employer violates Labor Law No. (6) of 2010, including cases where the worker is legally entitled to terminate the contract without notice (such as non-payment of wages, abuse, unsafe working conditions, fraud in contract terms, or false criminal accusations).

claim: Early transfer is allowed when the firm goes bankrupt or closes permanently
quote: The employment contract ends due to bankruptcy or permanent closure of the company, as defined under Article 50 of the law.

claim: Early transfer is allowed when the employer fails to complete residency or work-permit procedures through negligence
quote: The employer fails to issue or complete the worker’s residency or work permit procedures due to negligence, not the worker’s fault.

claim: The standard rule: transfer only after one year with the employer and with its consent
quote: Under the standard rule, expat employees are permitted to transfer jobs only after completing one year with their employer and with the employer’s consent.

claim: PAM first investigates the employer's violation before approving an early transfer
quote: PAM stated that in such disputed cases, it will first conduct an investigation to verify the employer’s violation before approving the transfer and imposing any necessary sanctions.

claim: Early transfer also when salaries are not transferred by the official procedure, or the worker wins a final court ruling
quote: workers can move to a new employer if salaries are not transferred in accordance with official procedures

claim: Ministerial decision A/57/2016 set KD 300 for transferring a worker brought for the private sector to another employer before completing one year

claim: KD 350 to move a worker from a government contract to the same employer's main file; KD 300 to another employer's government contract

quote: issued a decision setting the minimum monthly wage for workers in the private and oil sector at KD 75

quote: The announcement mandates that no residency or entry visa can be granted without proof of health insurance or a government/private health guarantee

quote: report any violations related to outdoor work during restricted hours by contacting the inspection team at 24936192

quote: Location: Hawally – Jabriya, Block 6, Street 104, Building 7, or any Labor Relations Department in your governorate.

quote: You can authorize someone in Kuwait (friend or lawyer) to file on your behalf.

quote: The court rejected all the arguments of the company and its requests regarding the absconding report, recruitment expenses and transfer of the employee.

claim: The company filed an absconding report after the worker asked for his dues
quote: he was surprised when the company filed an absconding report against him after he requested for his dues

claim: The Interior Minister can deport a foreigner even with a valid residence permit in cases set by the law
quote: empowers the Minister of Interior to issue a deportation order of any foreigner even if they hold a valid residence permit

claim: A foreigner ordered deported can be held up to 30 days, renewable
quote: can be detained for a period not exceeding 30 days, and is renewable if such detention is necessary

claim: The employer bears deportation costs, and anyone who employs, houses or harbours a foreigner bears all deportation costs
quote: obliges the breadwinner or employer to bear the expenses of deporting or removing a foreigner from Kuwait

claim: Decree-Law 114/2024 took effect on 5 January 2025
quote: The Ministry of Interior announced on Saturday that the residency decree-law 114/2024 for expatriates would take effect on Sunday.

claim: The law bans residency trading: recruiting or renewing visas or residence for money, for real or fictitious jobs; and employing a foreigner without authorisation
quote: It is strictly forbidden to engage in the trade of residency by exploiting the recruitment or facilitating the recruitment of a foreign individual

claim: Foreign workers must not work for anyone other than their employer without permission
quote: Foreign workers must not work for any party other than their designated employer without permission

claim: Employers may not assign workers to tasks other than those recruited for or let others employ them, or unjustifiably withhold dues
quote: Employers are also barred from unjustifiably withholding workers' dues.

claim: No one may shelter, employ or house a foreigner without valid residency
quote: it is prohibited for any individual to shelter, employ, or house a foreigner whose residency is invalid or expired

claim: Deportation despite valid residency is possible if the foreigner has no legitimate income, breaks Article 19, or for public interest, security or morality; it can extend to dependants
quote: Deportation orders for a foreigner may also extend to include family members who are financially dependent on the individual.

claim: Grounds: no legitimate source of income
quote: If the individual lacks a legitimate source of income.

claim: Violating Article 19 (working for others, unlawful employment) carries up to two years and/or KD 5,000-10,000
quote: Violations of Article 19 lead to imprisonment of up to two years, a fine of 5,000 to 10,000 Kuwaiti dinars, or both.

claim: Residency trading carries 3-5 years and/or KD 5,000-10,000, multiplied per foreigner
quote: Anyone violating Article 18 faces imprisonment for three to five years, a fine of 5,000 to 10,000 Kuwaiti dinars, or both.

claim: Those who receive permits in exchange for money face up to one year and/or up to KD 1,000; informants are exempt
quote: Those receiving permits in exchange for monetary compensation, benefits, or promises face imprisonment of up to one year, a fine of up to 1,000 Kuwaiti dinars, or both. Informants reporting such crimes are exempt from punishment.

claim: Previously deported foreigners may return only with the Interior Minister's explicit approval
quote: Previously deported foreigners may only return to Kuwait with explicit approval from the Minister of Interior.

claim: Foreign residents must show their passport on request and report loss or damage within two weeks

quote: they must leave Kuwait within a period set by the Ministry of Interior, not exceeding six months

claim: Late residency after entering on a work visa: KD 2 a day the first month, KD 4 after, capped at KD 1,200
